text:
DevOps Bot: INCIDENT ALERT — gpu-queue-backlog HIGH in prod (>= 90th percentile queue growth). Triggered by 2141598765
Maya (oncall): I'm on it, paging infra. Queue is growing across us-west-2 GPU pools, latency spiking for several hosted customers.
Eng Pager: paged Connor (infra) and Priya (sre) — @Connor @Priya please ack. :pager:
Connor (infra): ack. looking at autoscaler metrics + ASG events now. Can someone post the top-of-queue trace?
Maya (oncall): past 15m: queued requests jumped from ~200 -> 3.4k, token backlog ~48k. Affected routes: /v1/generate-gpu and /v1/chat-stream. Customers: small set of hosted-prod customers and a few PLG traffic spikes.
Priya (sre): grabbing logs from cluster-autoscaler and aws-asg-controller.
Kai (eng-runtime): I'm seeing a ton of throttling errors from our request queue processor (rate-limit to GPUs). Confirming autoscaler attempted scale up but number of Ready GPU nodes didn't increase.
Connor (infra): found repeated AttachInstanceProfile errors in CloudTrail for nodegroup "gpu-pool-prod-1":
```
2026-03-15T03:10:12Z ERROR AttachRolePolicy: AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::123456:assumed-role/kops-... not authorized to perform: iam:AttachRolePolicy
```
Looks like the launch template version was updated last night and the instance profile/iam permissions don't match. Nodes spin up then get tainted or fail to join.
Maya (oncall): that explains nodes launching but not becoming schedulable. Any immediate mitigation?
Connor (infra): we can try two things: 1) roll back launch template to v3 (known good) or 2) increase CPU-only fallback pool and steer some non-GPU workloads there. Rolling back requires a quick test; I'll try to roll back to last working LT version.
Priya (sre): autoscaler logs show scale events but kubelet registration failing with taint application errors. snippet:
```
W0315 03:11:22 scale_up.go:98] NodeGroup gpu-prod: launched instance i-0abcd but kubelet not ready (taint apply failed)
Error: node "ip-10-0-1-23" taint apply: failed to add taint: admission denied
```
So ASG created instances but nodes are NotReady and tainted, scheduler can't place pods.
Connor (infra): rolling LT to v3 now. I'll annotate the node group and trigger a small test scale up.
Alex (customer-facing): heads up to CS: I've DM'd support about impacted customer segments and flagged possible SLA violations. Need ETA to share.
Maya (oncall): updating status page: "Partial degradation for GPU-backed inference routes. Engineers investigating."
(3m later)
Connor (infra): rolled launch template to v3 and bumped ASG desired from 4->8 for the gpu pool. Starting to see new instances boot.
Priya (sre): kubelet logs on new instance show successful registration, taint applied correctly now. Pods starting to schedule on GPUs.
Kai (eng-runtime): we still have a backlog; the scheduler is draining the queue but rate will be limited for a bit. Recommending temporary rate limiting on non-critical routes to prioritize high-value traffic.
Maya (oncall): implementing route-level throttles for experimental customers. @Alex please coordinate customer comms.
Alex (customer-facing): will notify top 5 affected customers with temporary mitigation steps and ETA ~20-30m.
Eng Pager: confirmed on-call handoff to Connor at 03:30 UTC for infra follow-through. :arrow_right: @Connor (infra) you're the primary until we stabilize.
Connor (infra): acknowledged handoff. I will also open a support case with AWS for the AttachRolePolicy failures to audit why the new LT lost permissions.
Priya (sre): creating incident doc and adding short-term mitigations: 1) rollback LT (done), 2) temporarily increase GPU ASG desired capacity (done), 3) route throttling on non-critical customers (in progress), 4) escalate to cloud support for IAM change reasons.
Maya (oncall): monitoring metrics: queue down from 3.4k -> 820 in 12m, latency 95th reduced from 12s -> 3.6s. Still not fully recovered but trending.
Connor (infra): AWS case opened (case# 987654321). AWS support suggests the LT version change removed instance profile reference due to automated GitOps CFN change. We'll audit our pipeline to prevent accidental LT rewrites.
Priya (sre): addendum: one of the kube-proxy pods crashed on a new node causing transient network issues; restarted by k8s, didn't block scheduling long-term.
Maya (oncall): handing off monitoring to Priya at 03:46 UTC — Priya you own until recovery is verified and postmortem started.
Priya (sre): ack. I'll keep the status page updated and collect logs for postmortem. Next steps: run a quick runbook: validate LT permissions, lock LT auto-updates for GPU nodegroups, add pre-deploy gate to prevent iam/profile removal, and add autoscaler probe to detect taint-apply failures.
Connor (infra): I'll create a hotfix to the GitOps pipeline to stop automatic LT version bumping for GPU groups and add an IAM policy validation step.
Alex (customer-facing): CS notified customers, some asked for ETA/credits. Logged for postmortem.
Maya (oncall): current status: degraded -> partial recovery. Will close paging when queue < 200 and no new scale events failing.
Priya (sre): creating incident ticket with timeline and owners. We'll schedule postmortem with infra + runtime + devex tomorrow.
Connor (infra): noted. tagging follow-ups: infra (LT gating), security (IAM review), devex (runbook updates).
Maya (oncall): thanks team. I'll update the incident channel and close the thread when all tasks are handed off and metrics stable. :white_check_mark:
